review: Independent round 3 delivery, runtime reliability, performance, operations security, portability and Render readiness
stage: Independent initial conclusions recorded before coordination or access to earlier reviews
summary: Three concrete operational issues found: realtime readiness can remain green through a blackholed publish connection, accepted PostgreSQL queries have no configured deadline, and anonymous roommate paging/candidate requests do unbounded synchronous work. Current Render blueprint passes current published JSON Schema; no blueprint contract mismatch found. Provider timeout checks pass. Deployment remains blocked by actual provider/budget/ingress/CI/restore acceptance, not YAML syntax.

findings.title: Realtime readiness does not probe or bound the Pub/Sub connection
findings.trigger: A Pub/Sub TCP connection remains open and isReady=true, but PUBLISH replies or inbound messages stop while independent auth and messaging quota connections remain healthy.
findings.impact: containPublishFailures catches only rejection; pending publishes have no deadline and no realtime probe is registered. The API readiness endpoint returns status=ok and distributed realtime, preventing Render health recovery for this partial failure. Repeated publications also retain pending driver work. Durable HTTP history reduces data-loss impact but does not certify live event delivery.
findings.reproduction: Actual redis@5 client connected to a local RESP fixture. Fixture deliberately stops PUBLISH responses, while answering PING and EVAL. After 250ms the publish promise is unresolved and isReady remains true; production HealthService.ready returns all checks ok. Source has no longer runtime publish deadline or Pub/Sub active probe.
findings.recommendation: Register a bounded probe of both Pub/Sub clients, bound pending publications, mark degraded on timeout, and discard/reset stale clients or otherwise ensure restart/recovery. Test recovery without relying on customer writes and preserve adapter subscription semantics.

findings.title: Readiness and payment recovery can retain accepted database queries indefinitely
findings.trigger: PostgreSQL accepts an established connection/query but never completes it (network blackhole, stuck server query, lock wait). The documented URL has connection_limit and pool_timeout but no socket_timeout.
findings.impact: A health request has no application deadline and cannot reach the Valkey checks until SELECT 1 finishes. pool_timeout only bounds pool acquisition. Running payment recovery can likewise remain set forever, preventing later scans after dependency recovery; shutdown awaits it until Render SIGKILL. Render detects the health request as failed after five seconds, but each incoming health request can retain an unresolved promise/query until disconnect or process termination.
findings.reproduction: Installed Prisma 6.19.3 client connected to a fresh minimal PostgreSQL wire fixture with connect_timeout=1,pool_timeout=1,connection_limit=1. Fixture completed startup/prepare/describe/bind, accepted Execute SELECT 1, and withheld query completion. Client remained unresolved at 6200ms. This exercises the real client/engine; it is not a real PostgreSQL database or provider acceptance test.
findings.recommendation: Enforce a deliberate finite Prisma query/socket deadline and require it in the production configuration guidance/gate. Keep the readiness total deadline below Render’s five-second window, avoid duplicate accumulating probes, and verify a failed query releases or replaces its connection and permits a later recovery scan.

findings.title: Public roommate paging and candidate detail still load and rank every active profile
findings.trigger: Anonymous clients repeatedly request a one-item or empty page, or a nonexistent candidate ID, as active owned-profile count grows.
findings.impact: The 80-item response cap bounds response size only: the database query has no take, the entire set is scored and sorted twice synchronously, and candidate detail repeats the same process. On this Mac, 50,000 profiles returned an empty page but blocked the event loop for about 192ms and grew heap by 85MB (RSS 360MB including TS runtime). Repeated requests share the API event loop with health, authentication, and messaging. No route-specific quota was found on these anonymous routes. Similar full-collection public listing/profile reads remain capacity limitations.
findings.recommendation: Bound database candidate selection and detail lookup, preserve documented ranking/discovery behavior within a bounded working set, and/or enforce a reviewed low-volume demo capacity/ingress quota until full discovery scaling is deliberately designed. Verify timer lag and DB query bounds; do not claim scalable paging from slice alone.
findings.limits: Synthetic in-memory scoring microbenchmark on macOS Node 25.8.0; excludes database, JSON serialization, network, and Render CPU measurement. Exact production capacity is unproven.
